questions.question: In India, "APEDA" is related to which of the following?
questions.solution:

__
 
• APEDA stands for the** Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority.**
 
• The Government of India established it **to promote the export of agricultural and processed food products.**
 
• APEDA is responsible for providing financial assistance, conducting training, and helping with the development of agricultural export standards.
 
• It plays a significant role in enhancing the global reach of Indian agricultural produce.
 
• APEDA is involved in promoting products such as** fruits, vegetables, meat, poultry, and various processed foods.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Arms and Ammunition:**

 
 
• The sector related to arms and ammunition is regulated by the Ministry of Home Affairs and Defense in India.
 
• Agencies like the **Ordnance Factory Board (OFB) and Defense Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) **focus on arms manufacturing and research.
 
 
 
• **IT Services:**
 
 
• The IT services sector in India is overseen by the** Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.**
 
• It includes major players in software development, IT outsourcing, and digital services.
 
 
 
• **Highways:**
 
 
• The development and maintenance of highways in India fall under the **Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.**
 
• Agencies like the **National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) **are involved in the construction of roads and highways.

questions.question: As of July 2023, who has become the second longest serving Chief Minister of an Indian states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Naveen Patnaik.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Naveen Patnaik, the **Chief Minister of Odisha**, became the **second-longest serving Chief Minister** of an Indian state as of July 2023.
 
• He has been serving as the Chief Minister **since March 2000**, consistently winning elections and leading the Biju Janata Dal (BJD).
 
• Patnaik is known for his focus on** social welfare schemes and disaster management**, which have garnered him widespread popularity.
 
• His tenure has seen significant development in infrastructure, education, and healthcare in Odisha.
 
• He is also recognized for maintaining a clean and corruption-free image throughout his political career.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1812ea40d45ce5e492dbd1c0879d1061a79cac2fc10623e5486043fbf578bf88.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shivraj Singh Chauhan:**

 
 
• Shivraj Singh Chauhan is the **Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh.**
 
• He has served multiple terms as CM, with his first term starting in 2005, but his total tenure is not as long as Naveen Patnaik’s.
 
• He is known for implementing various **agriculture and rural development programs.**
 
 
 
• **Yogi Adityanath:**
 
 
• Yogi Adityanath is the** Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh since 2017.**
 
• He is notable for his strong stance on law and order and promoting development projects in the state.
 
• His tenure is far shorter compared to Naveen Patnaik's.
 
 
 
• **Pawan Kumar Chamling:**
 
 
• Pawan Kumar Chamling was the** longest-serving Chief Minister of Sikkim,** having served from 1994 to 2019.
 
• He held the record as the longest-serving CM before Naveen Patnaik moved up to second place in terms of service length.
 
• Chamling is known for his work in** environmental preservation and social welfare** in Sikkim.

questions.question: What was India's literacy rate at the time of independence in 1947?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**12%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When the **British rule** ended in India in the year **1947**, the literacy rate was just around **12%**.
 
• The British rule in India refers to the period during which the Indian Subcontinent was under the colonial rule of the British Empire.
 
• It began in **1757**, following the** Battle of Plassey**, and continued until India gained independence on **August 15, 1947**.
 
• The British East India Company initially established a strong presence in India for trade, but over time, they gradually expanded their control over various **regions** and **Territories**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• According to the **2011 Census of India**, the overall rate of literacy is **73 percent**. But breaking up the national average reveals that while the rate of literacy for men is **80.9 **percent, for women it is** 65.46 percent**. This means that more than one-fourth of the country's population is still illiterate.
 
• Literacy forms an important input in the overall development of individuals enabling them to comprehend their social, political, and cultural environment better and respond to it appropriately.
 
• Higher levels of education and literacy lead to greater awareness and also contribute to the improvement of economic and social conditions.
 
• It acts as a catalyst for social upliftment enhancing the returns on investment made in almost every aspect of development effort, be it population control, health, hygiene, environmental degradation control, or employment of weaker sections of the society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The following are some of the important factors that could affect the low literacy rate of women in India-** 

 
 
• Poor school environment for girls 
 
• The lower enrolment 
 
• Dowry system 
 
• Early marriage
 
• Priority to the son’s education compared to the daughter’s education 
 
• Poverty

questions.question: The Sixth Economic Census of India was conducted in which of the following years?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2013**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Sixth Economic Census was conducted between **January 2013 and April 2014 across the country**. This census follows a series of **economic censuses conducted since 1977.**
 
• The census was conducted by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) in collaboration with state governments and union territories.
 
• The census collected comprehensive data from** all non-agricultural **enterprises involved in various sectors such as manufacturing, trade, services, and others.
 
• The main objective was to collect information on the distribution of economic establishments, including data on their nature of activity, employment, and ownership patterns. 
 
• The **Sixth Economic Census** was **crucial for understanding changes in the economic structure**, including the growth of small businesses, employment trends, and the contribution of the informal sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **First Economic Census:** Conducted in 1977, marking the beginning of comprehensive data collection on India's non-agricultural sector.
 
• **Second Economic Census**: Held in 1980, focusing on the growth and expansion of enterprises.
 
• **Third Economic Census**: Conducted in 1990, further refining data on establishments and employment.
 
• **Fourth Economic Census**: This took place in 1998, showing significant changes in the economic landscape post-liberalization.
 
• **Fifth Economic Census:** Conducted in 2005, focusing on the formal and informal sectors across urban and rural areas.
 
• **Seventh Economic Census**: Conducted in 2019, the latest in the series, focusing on digital data collection through mobile applications.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Economic Census Importance:** Provides a comprehensive database for understanding economic activities, particularly in the informal sector, which employs a large portion of India’s workforce.
 
• **Key Data Collected:** Types of enterprises, employment numbers, ownership details, and enterprise activity classifications.
 
• The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation **(MoSPI) leads the Economic Census**, coordinating with state governments.
 
• The data aids in policy formulation for economic development programs like Make in India, Startup India, and Skill India.

• The** Services team**, which had won the last four editions of the Games **finished second **with 126 medals: 66 gold, 27 silver, and 33 bronze.
 
• **Haryana secured the third position** with 192 medals, including 62 gold, 55 silver, and 75 bronze.
 
• Srihari Nataraj, an Olympic swimmer, was named the best male athlete, with a haul of 8 gold, 1 silver, and 1 bronze.

• **First National Games**: Held in **1924 in Lahore,** British India, originally called the Indian Olympic Games.
 
• The National Games are held every few years, though they have faced several delays due to logistical and other challenges.

• The National Games feature a wide variety of sports, including athletics, swimming, wrestling, shooting, gymnastics, and more, covering both Olympic and non-Olympic sports.

• The National Games serve as a platform for talent identification, promoting sportsmanship and preparing athletes for international competitions like the Olympics.

questions.question: Gautama Buddha decided to find his own path to realisation, and meditated for days on end under a ________ tree at Bodh Gaya in Bihar.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Peepal**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Gautama Buddha meditated under a **Bodhi tree (Ficus religiosa), also known as Peepal**, which is now a sacred symbol in Buddhism.
 
• This event took place at Bodh Gaya, located in the state of Bihar, India.
 
• Under this tree, **Buddha attained enlightenment or nirvana,** which marked a key turning point in his spiritual journey.
 
• Buddha meditated for days on end, showing his commitment to finding the path to self-realization and truth.
 
• The site, Bodh Gaya, is now one of the most important pilgrimage destinations for **Buddhists worldwide.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gautama Buddha**

 
 
• Gautama Buddha was born as **Siddhartha Gautama around 563 BCE in Lumbini**, present-day Nepal, into a royal family of the Shakya clan.
 
• Renunciation: At **the age of 29,** after witnessing suffering in the form of old age, sickness, and death (the Four Sights), he renounced his princely life to seek a solution to human suffering.
 
• Buddha attained enlightenment (nirvana) under the** Bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya, Bihar,** after meditating for 49 days. This event is central to Buddhist teachings.
 
• After attaining enlightenment, Buddha delivered his first sermon at Sarnath (also known as the Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta), where he taught the Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path.
 
• Buddha's key teachings include the** Four Noble Truths** (existence of suffering, cause of suffering, end of suffering, and the path to the end of suffering) and the Eightfold Path (a guide to ethical and mental development).
 
• He **emphasized the Middle Path**, avoiding extremes of asceticism and indulgence, advocating a balanced approach to life.
 
• Buddha taught in Pali and Magadhi, the languages of the common people, to make his teachings accessible.
 
• Buddha established a community of monks and nuns, known as the Sangha, which played a crucial role in spreading Buddhism.
 
• Buddha **passed away around 483 BCE in Kushinagar**, Uttar Pradesh, at the age of 80, attaining Parinirvana.
 
• His teachings led to the rise of Buddhism, which spread across Asia, particularly in countries like **Sri Lanka, China, Japan, and Southeast Asia.**

questions.question: The spring festival of Holi is celebrated as Yaoshang by the Meitei tribe in the state of ________, lasting about six days.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Manipur**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Yaoshang lasts for about **six days, typically **coinciding with the full moon of the **Lai Haraoba **month, which falls in **March, marking the arrival of spring.**
 
• The festival celebrates the arrival of spring and is deeply rooted in the **agricultural traditions** of the Meitei tribe, symbolizing new beginnings and prosperity.
 
• During Yaoshang, various traditional activities take place, **including singing, dancing, and playing traditional sports** like Mukna (a form of wrestling). The community comes together for cultural performances, reinforcing social bonds.
 
• Yaoshang is akin to the Holi festival celebrated across India, where colors are thrown, but in Manipur, it also includes unique local practices, such as the '**Wangala' dance and the 'Chavang Kut' ritual.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Festival**
 **Significance**
 
 

 Lai Haraoba
 Celebrates the **Gods and Spirits** of the Meitei tribe; features dance and music rituals.
 
 

 Cheiraoba
 Marks the **New Year; involves feasting** and preparation of traditional dishes.
 
 

 Kang Festival
 Celebrates the arrival of the **monsoon season**; includes offerings to local deities.
 
 

 Ningol Chakouba
 A festival reinforcing bonds between **brothers and sisters** through communal feasting.
 
 

 Mera Houchongba
 A cultural festival showcasing dances and competitions to **promote unity among communities.**

questions.question: Which of the following Acts allowed detention of political prisoners without trial for two years?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rowalatt Act**__.

__
 
• The Rowlatt Act, officially known as the Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes** Act of 1919.**
 
• The primary purpose of the Rowlatt Act was to curb revolutionary activities and **suppress political dissent in India.**
 
• It allowed for detention** without trial for up to two years.**
 
• During the enactment of the Rowlatt Act in 1919, the **Governor-General of India was Lord Chelmsford.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Arms Act of 1959** in India is a significant piece of legislation governing the possession, use, and control of firearms and ammunition.
 
• The** Arms Act was enacted on September 28, 1959**.
 
• The **Vernacular Press Act of 1878** was a significant piece of legislation enacted by the British government in India.
 
• The Act was enacted on** March 14, 1878**, during the tenure of** Lord Lytton**, who was the Viceroy of India at that time.
 
• The** Government of India Act of 1935** was a landmark piece of legislation enacted by the British Parliament to define the governance of India.
 
• The Act is **comprised of 303 sections and 10 schedules.**

questions.question: Article 163 of the Indian Constitution is related to which of the following?

options.text: Conduct of Business of the Government of a State
Council of Ministers to aid and advise Governor

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Council of Ministers to aid and advise Governor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 74**: Council of Ministers to Aid and Advise the President.
 
• **Article 76**: Attorney General for India
 
• **Article 77**: Conduct of Business of the Government of India.
 
• **Article 78**: Duties of Prime Minister as a Head of the Government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 168 **Provides for the establishment of a Legislature in each State, which may be unicameral or bicameral.
 
• **Article 169** Empowers Parliament to create or abolish a State Legislature, which may be either a Legislative Council or Legislative Assembly.
 
• **Article 170** Specifies the composition of the State Legislative Assembly, which consists of representatives elected by the people.
 
• **Article 171** Details the composition of the State Legislative Council, including the method of election and appointment of its members.
 
• **Article 172** States the duration of the State Legislative Assembly, which is five years from the date of its first meeting unless dissolved earlier.
 
• **Article 173** Specifies the qualifications for membership in the State Legislatures.
 
• **Article 174** Grants the Governor the power to summon and prorogue the State Legislature and to dissolve the Legislative Assembly.

questions.question: Which measure captures the difference between the government's total expenditure and total receipts, excluding borrowing?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fiscal Deficit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The measure that captures the **difference between the government's total expenditure and total receipts**, excluding borrowing, is known as the Fiscal Deficit.
 
• Fiscal deficit occurs when a government's total expenditures exceed its total revenues (excluding borrowing).
 
• **Fiscal Deficit=Total Expenditure−Total Receipts (excluding borrowing).**
 
• **Revenue Deficit**: This is a subset of the fiscal deficit that focuses specifically on the gap between revenue expenditure and revenue receipts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Primary deficit refers to the difference between the government's total expenditure (excluding interest payments) and its total revenue (excluding borrowing).
 
• **Primary Deficit**=Fiscal Deficit−Interest Payments.
 
• Gross Fiscal Deficit is the difference between the total expenditure of the government and its total receipts (excluding borrowings)
 
• **Gross Fiscal Deficit**=Total Expenditure−Total Receipts (excluding borrowing).
 
• Revenue deficit refers to the excess of the government's revenue expenditure over its revenue receipts in a given fiscal period.
 
• **Revenue Deficit**=Revenue Expenditure−Revenue Receipts.

questions.question: Ghoomar dance is associated with which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Ghoomar.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ghoomar is a traditional folk dance of **state of Rajasthan.**
 
• The name **Ghoomar **is derived from the word **ghoomna**, which means spinning or twirling.
 
• Ghoomar is performed on traditional Rajasthani folk music, with its rhythmic beats.
 
• Common instruments include: the **Dhol (drum), Nagada, Shehnai, and Harmonium.**
 
• It is performed on occasions such as weddings, festivals **like Teej, Gangaur, and Diwali, as well as other celebrations.**
 
• The dance symbolizes **joy and togetherness, communal harmony and social unity, **with **women of all ages participating together.**
